full_judgment:
11. The appellate Court dismissed the Title Suit No. 103 of 1990 on the finding that plaintiff failed to establish his case of entering into an agreement with Amir All Khan for purchase of the land in suit and that also failed to establish that the said bainapatra was burned. The appellate Court in Appeal No. 289 of 1990 arrived at the finding that the money receipt and the solenama were created collusively. 

 13. The learned Counsel for the petitioner submits that the High Court Division was in error in concurring with the finding arrived at by the court of appeal below that plaintiff of Title Suit No. 103 of 1990 failed to establish his case of entering into an agreement for sale of the land by Amir Ali Khan and that in concurring with the finding that the solenama and the money receipt were the product of collusion of the defendant Nos. 1 and 4 of the said suit. This submission of the learned Counsel merits no consideration since he failed to point out that the finding arrived at as to the case of the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 103 of 1990 relating to agreement for sale said to have been entered into by Amir Ali Khan is not based on evidence or that has been made on misleading or non consideration of the evidence and other materials on record.
